claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who lives with me at home. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions:

First, how old is Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of their exact age at the moment - they're somewhere between 15 and 19. I can find out the exact age if you need it, but would that range help for now?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. The exact age is important because there are different rules that apply depending on whether a young person is under or over 16, and eligibility generally stops at age 20 (or earlier in some cases).

Could you please confirm Alex's exact age? This will help me determine which rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: You know what, let me check their birth certificate when I get home - I don't have the exact date with me right now. Is there anything else you can help me figure out in the meantime, or do you need that exact age before we can go any further?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! While the age is important, I can gather some other information in the meantime that will help with the assessment.

Let me ask you this: Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, are they attending school, college, or an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that either, to be honest. They might be, but I'd need to double-check what they're doing at the moment. Is there anything else you need to know that I might be able to answer now?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
No problem! Let me ask you about your own circumstances then.

Are you currently responsible for Alex? That is, do they live with you and are you the person who is mainly responsible for them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives with me at home and I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you!

Now, let me ask about your immigration status and residence: Are you living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status or another immigration status that allows you to live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in England. I have the right to live here, no issues with that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One more question about your circumstances: Are you or your partner (if you have one) subject to immigration control? This means having conditions on your stay in the UK that prevent you from claiming public funds.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that - there are no restrictions on claiming public funds or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you.

Now, to complete the assessment for Alex, I do need to come back to those earlier questions about their age and education/training status, as these are crucial for determining eligibility.

Child Benefit rules state that:
- You can generally claim for children under 16
- You can claim for young people aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or approved training

Since Alex is somewhere between 15 and 19, their exact age and whether they're in education or training will determine their eligibility.

When you're able to confirm Alex's exact age and whether they're currently in approved education or training, I'll be able to give you a definitive answer about your eligibility. Would you be able to find out this information and get back to me?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand. Look, I really need to know about this now if possible. Let me think... I know they're definitely somewhere in that 15-19 range, but I genuinely can't remember their exact birthday right now. And as for education or training, I'm just not certain what their current status is - they might be studying, they might not be, I'd have to ask them or check some paperwork at home.

Is there really no way to give me at least a general idea of whether I might be eligible? Or do you absolutely need those specific details before you can tell me anything?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you'd like an answer now, and I appreciate your situation. Let me explain what I can tell you based on what we know:

**What we know so far that's positive:**
- Alex lives with you and you're responsible for them ✓
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here ✓
- You have no restrictions on claiming public funds ✓

**The challenge is:**
The age and education/training status are not just helpful details - they're the core criteria that determine eligibility for Alex specifically. Here's why:

- **If Alex is under 16**: You would likely be eligible regardless of education status
- **If Alex is 16-19 AND in approved education/training**: You would likely be eligible
- **If Alex is 16-19 AND NOT in approved education/training**: You would NOT be eligible

So with Alex being "somewhere between 15-19" and education status unknown, there are scenarios where you'd be eligible and scenarios where you wouldn't be. I genuinely cannot give you a definitive answer without these key facts.

Would you be able to make a quick call to Alex or check any school/college correspondence you might have at hand? Or confirm even just whether they're still at school age (under 16) versus older?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alright, I hear you. Look, I really can't confirm those details right now - I don't have access to the information you need at this moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. Once you have Alex's exact age and can confirm whether they're in education or training (if they're 16 or over), I'll be able to give you a clear answer on your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Once you have this information, please come back and I'll be able to complete the assessment and let you know definitively whether you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Once you have Alex's age and education/training status, I'll be here to help you complete the assessment.

Take care, and I look forward to helping you when you return with that information!
